Release.hintMovedOn.source: We still expect to see them at another gathering.

Release.hintDeparted.source: Graduated, moved away, or stopped coming — this is the resolution.

Release.noteHint.source: Kept on the record under this list, for whoever reads it later.

Release.consequenceDeparted.source: Marking {name} “no longer with us” means Tally stops asking about them: they leave this list and will not appear on any other. Checking them in here again undoes it.

Release.consequenceDepartedUnseen.source: {name} has not been seen at any gathering since {date}. Marking {name} “no longer with us” means Tally stops asking about them: they leave this list and will not appear on any other. Checking them in here again undoes it.

Release.consequenceMovedOn.source: {name} leaves this list now and stays on the ministry's radar: if no gathering sees them, they will appear under “Not seen at any gathering” after about {threshold} more gatherings. Checking them in here again undoes the release by itself.

Release.consequenceMovedOnUnseen.source: {name} has not been seen at any gathering since {date}. {name} leaves this list now and stays on the ministry's radar: if no gathering sees them, they will appear under “Not seen at any gathering” after about {threshold} more gatherings. Checking them in here again undoes the release by itself.

Settings.ruleNote.source: Each series counts only its own history — Friday never predicts Sunday. A brand-new series relaxes the threshold to whatever history exists, so the block is never empty for the wrong reason.

Settings.errWindowTooSmall.source: Cannot ask for more gatherings than the window holds.

Backends.fromDeploy.source: These settings came with the deploy. Changing any of them here takes over from it.

Backends.pcoDescription.source: Where Tally reads your people from. It keeps no copy of them.

Backends.pcoAskFailed.source: Could not ask Tally about the connection.

Backends.pcoRefreshed.source: Read the roster again from Planning Center

Backends.pcoRefreshFailed.source: Could not refresh from Planning Center.

Backends.pcoWriteOff.source: Tally never writes to Planning Center. Visitors stay queued until this is turned on.

Backends.pcoWriteCreate.source: Tally creates people it has not seen before, but never edits an existing one.

Backends.pcoWriteFull.source: Tally creates people, and Edit profile saves a linked student’s name, grade and allergies straight to Planning Center. It can also add an adult — creating the household if there is none — and put a phone number or email on them.

Backends.pcoCacheOff.source: Caching is off. Every screen asks Planning Center directly — slower, and always current.

Backends.pcoCacheOn.source: An answer is reused for up to {count, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} before Tally asks Planning Center again.

Backends.pcoRosterNote.source: Who is on the roster is Tally's own list — add and remove students on the Students screen. Planning Center supplies their names, grades and parent contact, and Tally stores none of it.

Backends.pcoUnresolved.source: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} on the roster but can no longer be read from Planning Center — deleted or merged upstream.

Backends.pcoQueuedWriteOff.source: {count, plural, one {# student has} other {# students have}} no Planning Center person yet — and none will be created while write-back is off.

Backends.pcoQueued.source: {count, plural, one {# student has} other {# students have}} no Planning Center person yet. Push them from the Queued badge on their roster row.

Backends.pcoRosterOffline.source: This device is showing a roster it saved earlier. Check-in still works; anyone added since will not appear until Planning Center is reachable again.

Backends.secretManagerNote.source: The credentials themselves live in Secret Manager and are not editable from the app.

Backends.a32Description.source: A second place Tally can read people from, beside Planning Center.

Backends.a32AskFailed.source: Could not ask Tally about the connections.

Backends.a32Refreshed.source: Read the roster again from every connected backend

Backends.a32WriteOff.source: Tally never writes to Attendees. Visitors stay queued until this is turned on.

Backends.a32WriteCreate.source: Tally creates attendees it has not seen before, but never edits an existing one.

Backends.a32WriteFull.source: Tally creates attendees, and Edit profile saves a linked student’s name, grade, allergies and birthday straight to Attendees. It can also add an adult to the family and fill in their phone or email.

Backends.a32RosterNote.source: Students added from Attendees keep their Attendees record as the source of their name, grade and family — exactly as Planning Center students do theirs.

Backends.a32Unresolved.source: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} on the roster but can no longer be read from Attendees — removed upstream.

Backends.a32NothingConnected.source: Nothing is connected yet. Run the setup command on your Attendees server, put its token in Secret Manager, then enter the addresses and slugs it prints under Change.

Backends.tokenNote.source: The token itself lives in Secret Manager and is not editable from the app.

Backends.newStudentsDescription.source: Which system a student created in Tally — a quick-add at the door — is pushed to.

Backends.defaultChangeFailed.source: Could not change where new students go.

Backends.queuedGoingTo.source: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} queued and will go to {backend} on the next push.

Backends.notMoved.source: Students already linked to a backend are not moved by this — it decides only where a brand-new student's record is created.

Backends.heldForReview.source: {count, plural, one {# student registered themselves at the kiosk and is waiting for somebody to approve them.} other {# students registered themselves at the kiosk and are waiting for somebody to approve them.}}

Backends.gradeRangeError.source: Cannot end below where it starts.

Backends.pcoGradeBandNote.source: Who is on the roster is decided on the Students screen, one student at a time. This band only says where a student Planning Center has no grade for lands, and it is the range the app understands at all.

Backends.pcoWriteHintOff.source: Tally never writes to Planning Center. Visitors added at the door stay queued until this is turned on.

Backends.pcoWriteHintCreate.source: Tally creates people it has not seen before, after searching for a match. It never edits an existing person.

Backends.pcoWriteHintFull.source: Tally creates people, and Edit profile becomes editable for students Planning Center already has — first name, last name, grade and medical notes are saved there. A leader can also add an adult, and the household if there is none. It offers anybody Planning Center already has by that name before creating a second record, and never overwrites a number on file.

Backends.pcoCacheHintOff.source: Off. Every screen asks Planning Center directly — slower, and always current.

Backends.pcoCacheHintOn.source: Eight counselors opening Tally in the same minute cost one read instead of eight. A name corrected in Planning Center appears within {seconds} seconds.

Backends.pcoApiAddressHint.source: Leave empty to use whatever the deploy configured — currently {url}. Every request carries this church's credentials, so any other address sends them somewhere else: set this only for a proxy you run, or a test rig.

Backends.a32WriteHintOff.source: Tally never writes to Attendees. Visitors added at the door stay queued until this is turned on.

Backends.a32WriteHintCreate.source: Tally creates attendees it has not seen before, after searching for a match. It never edits an existing one.

Backends.a32WriteHintFull.source: Tally creates attendees, and Edit profile becomes editable for students Attendees already has — name, grade, allergies and birthday are saved there. A leader can also add an adult to the family, and fill in their phone or email when Attendees has none.

Backends.a32ConnectedHint.source: Attendees serves the roster alongside any other connected backend.

Backends.a32DisconnectedHint.source: Switched off. Students already linked to Attendees stay on the roster but their names cannot be read until this is turned back on.

Backends.a32SlugsNote.source: Where your students live in Attendees. The setup command on the Attendees side prints all four — they name the division and meet whose attendees are the roster, and the character new students join.

Backends.a32GradeBandNote.source: The band a student with no grade in Attendees lands in, and the range the app understands at all.

Backends.a32CacheHintOff.source: Off. Every screen asks Attendees directly — slower, and always current.

Backends.a32CacheHintOn.source: Eight counselors opening Tally in the same minute cost one read instead of eight. A name corrected in Attendees appears within {seconds} seconds.

Backends.a32ApiAddressHint.source: Where your Attendees server lives. Every request carries this church's token, so any other address sends it somewhere else — admins only, and only for a server you run.

Team.description.source: Who may sign in to Tally, and what they may do once they have. Changes apply to every phone immediately.

Team.howSummary.source: How Tally decides who may sign in

Team.howBody.source: Tally decides access by Google address. An admin invites somebody here, they sign in with that Google account, and their profile appears beside this — from then on the profile decides what they may do. Some admins are pinned by the deployment itself and cannot be changed here; that is the way back in if access is ever lost.

Team.membersDescription.source: Outstanding invitations are not listed here.

Team.membersEmptyBody.source: Invite a Google address above, or sign in with one of the addresses named in TALLY_ADMIN_EMAILS.

Team.otherAdminOnly.source: Another admin has to change this.

Team.invitesDescription.source: Addresses that may sign in but have not yet.

Team.googleAddressHint.source: It has to be the Google account they will actually sign in with — Tally matches on the address.

Team.invitesEmptyBody.source: Everybody who has been invited has signed in.

Team.withdrawWarning.source: This deletes the invitation for good.

KioskPair.intro.source: On the kiosk device, open <mono>/kiosk</mono>. It shows a six-character code — type it here to sign that kiosk in as you.

KioskPair.whatIsKiosk.source: <mono>/kiosk</mono> is a self-serve screen for a device in the lobby, served on this same site: families check themselves in by name, or by the last four digits of a household phone number.

KioskPair.retire.source: To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data on the device.

KioskPair.retireCore.source: To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data on the device — or deactivate and reactivate your account to cut every session loose.

KioskPair.blocked.source: This deployment cannot sign a kiosk in. Approving a code still records it, but the lobby screen keeps waiting until the role below is granted.

KioskPair.codeHint.source: Codes last ten minutes. If this one is refused, read the code the kiosk is showing now and try again.

KioskPair.outcomeApproved.source: Approved — the kiosk signs itself in on its next poll, and every check-in it records will be under your name.

KioskPair.outcomeNotFound.source: No kiosk is showing that code. Codes last ten minutes; read the one on the kiosk screen now — the letters I, L, O and the digits 0 and 1 never appear.

KioskPair.outcomeExpired.source: That code has expired. The kiosk is already showing a fresh one — read it off the screen and try again.

KioskPair.outcomeFailed.source: Could not reach the server. Try again in a moment.

KioskPair.signingOk.source: Tally can hand a kiosk a session. It says nothing about the screen in the lobby.

KioskPair.copyFailed.source: Could not copy — select the command below instead.

KioskPair.stuckPending.source: Once the role is granted, these are the remaining reasons a kiosk keeps waiting.

KioskPair.stuckHomeScreen.source: A kiosk installed to the device's home screen keeps its own storage, so it asks to be paired a second time.

KioskPair.stuckDeactivated.source: A kiosk stops when its approver's access is deactivated. Pair it again from an active account.

KioskPair.phoneSearchNote.source: Only the last four digits of a household's numbers are ever stored in Tally. The index rebuilds nightly on its own; use this when a family's number changed today.

KioskPair.rebuilt.source: Phone search rebuilt: {students} students, {entries} number endings.

KioskPair.rebuildFailed.source: Could not rebuild the kiosk phone index. Is a people backend reachable?
